narrative.intro: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $10.9B in contracts in FY2026 to date. The agency recorded 6,508 awards with an average award size of $1.7M, and obligations are down 30.9% year over year. Annual obligations were $15B in FY21, $15.2B in FY22, $16.1B in FY23, $15B in FY24, and $15.8B in FY25, before the current FY26-to-date total of $10.9B. Research and development categories dominate spending, led by Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) at $4.2B. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing accounts for $1.7B, and several other NAICS categories, including Engineering Services at $665M and Facilities Support Services at $389M, make up the remainder of the top categories. CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY received $1.7B, followed by THE BOEING COMPANY at $1B, and a mix of university labs and prime contractors fill the rest of the top-ten vendor list.

sections.heading: How has the agency's contracting changed year over year?
sections.body: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $10.9B in FY2026 to date, down 30.9% year over year. Annual obligations were $15B in FY21, $15.2B in FY22, $16.1B in FY23, $15B in FY24, and $15.8B in FY25, showing a lower FY26-to-date total compared with prior full years. The agency has 6,508 awards so far in FY2026 with an average award size of $1.7M.

sections.heading: Where are the agency's contract dollars concentrated?
sections.body: Research and development in the physical, engineering, and life sciences is the largest NAICS category at $4.2B. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing accounts for $1.7B, and other notable categories include Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) at $666M, Engineering Services at $665M, and Facilities Support Services at $389M. The top vendors include CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY at $1.7B and THE BOEING COMPANY at $1B, with university labs and large primes rounding out the top ten.

faq.q: How much does National Aeronautics and Space Administration spend on contracts?
faq.a: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $10.9B in contracts in FY2026 to date. The agency recorded 6,508 awards with an average award size of $1.7M, and obligations are down 30.9% year over year. Historical annual obligations were $15B in FY21, $15.2B in FY22, $16.1B in FY23, $15B in FY24, and $15.8B in FY25.

faq.q: What does National Aeronautics and Space Administration buy?
faq.a: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration buys a lot of research and development, led by Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) at $4.2B. The agency also obligates funds to Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing at $1.7B, Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Biotechnology) at $666M, Engineering Services at $665M, and Facilities Support Services at $389M, among other categories.

faq.q: Who are National Aeronautics and Space Administration's largest contractors?
faq.a: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration's largest contractors are CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY at $1.7B and THE BOEING COMPANY at $1B. Other top contractors include THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY APPLIED PHYSICS LABORATORY LLC at $470M, LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP at $400M, KBR WYLE SERVICES, LLC at $339M, NORTHROP GRUMMAN SYSTEMS CORPORATION at $337M, AEROJET ROCKETDYNE OF DE, INC at $324M, BLUE ORIGIN MANUFACTURING, LLC at $300M, AMENTUM TECHNOLOGY, INC. at $279M, and BAE SYSTEMS SPACE & MISSION SYSTEMS INC. at $215M.
